newsitem.title: USA: NYMEX Hub natgas ends lower but Apr holds support.
newsitem.headline: NYMEX Hub natgas ends lower but Apr holds support.

text.p: NYMEX Hub natgas futures settled marginally lower Tuesday following a sluggish, range-bound afternoon session, as softer cash prices put some early downward pressure on the market, industry sources said.

Trading in only a four-cent range, April finished 1.2 cents lower at $1.897 per mmBtu after testing a low of $1.87 early in the session. Likewise, May ended down 1.3 cents at $1.935, while other deferreds were remained little changed.
"Cash was down early, and the weather looks like it's only going to get warmer as the weekend nears. If cash falls again tomorrow, we should expect a break through $1.87," one said.

Temperatures in the East and parts of the Midwest are forecast to remain cold through Saturday but then return to near-normal levels by Sunday. Warmer-than-normal weather is expected to continue throughout most of the West, Weather Services Corp said.

In its six- to 10-day forecast, Weather Services Corp is expecting below-normal temperatures across the upper Northwest, the northern and southern plains and the upper Northeast. Warmer-than-normal weather is forecast for the Southeast and the northern California coast.

Technically, support in April was still seen at $1.85-1.87, and then at $1.78-1.80 and the $1.701 contract low. Minor resistance was seen at $1.94-1.95. Further resistance was pegged at $2, and then in the mid-teens and at $2.28.
Taking a look ahead, traders are pegging May support at $1.845 and resistance at $2.00-2.05.
The 12-month strip fell 0.6 cent to $2.059. NYMEX said an estimated 29,965 Henry Hub contracts traded as of 1450 EST, compared with Monday's revised tally of 36,944.

In the cash market, Gulf Coast prices remained in convergence with futures, falling an average of 10 cents to the high-$1.80s to low-$1.90s. Prices on the Midcontinent pipes were down more than 10 cents to the mid-$1.70s to about $1.80, with Detroit city-gate talked around $2.16-2.17. At the New York city-gate, prices held in the mid-$2.30s to low-$2.40s.
Withdrawal estimates for Wednesday's American Gas Association storage report range anywhere from 10 to 90 bcf, with most at the lower end. Year-ago inventories fell 72 bcf.
No NYMEX Permian and Alberta natgas traded today.
On the KCBT, April settled a half-cent lower at $1.70. Deferreds were a half-cent to one cent lower. The East/West spread narrowed by 0.8 cent to 19.7 cents (NYMEX premium).
Physical cash prices in the Permian Basin were talked at least five cents lower in the low-to-mid $1.70s, while the Waha market softened by a similar amount to the high-$1.70s.
